text:
This is the part people don’t show enough about AI game dev on X.

Behind every “Fable 5 made me a full game in one prompt” post, there’s usually a lot of bullshit.

I gave AI a strong /goal:
optimized Three.js grass, chunks, LOD, shader wind.
It produced something.
It understood part of the direction.

But it still missed.
That’s the real workflow.

A prompt can give you a starting point.
It doesn’t magically give you taste, debugging, optimization, and iteration.

You can test the /goal below.

author: dfxoqeth
text:
A 24-year-old in Chengdu made 71,400 yuan (~$9,800) last month from 47 mobile games

He never wrote more than 200 lines of code in his life

Claude Fable 5 wrote the other 800,000

Total Claude spend for 11 weeks: 1,847 yuan

Pause at 3:02. That is not a Mario emulator. That is a working clone of Super Mario 1-1 built in 4 minutes 58 seconds. Pixel-perfect art. Original physics. NES color palette. Custom font. Level data. Full game engine. 1,213 lines of game.js. 149 lines of level.js. All generated in one session

He did not run it as a fan project

He repainted the sprites. Renamed Mario to something the store would approve. Changed the green pipes to red. Shipped it on TapTap as "Mushroom Adventure."

It made 4,200 yuan in the first week

He shipped 6 more variants the same month

By month 2 he had 12 games live. By month 3 he had 47

The games are not masterpieces. He knows that. They do not need to be. They need to be cheap, fun, and finished.
The Chinese App Store does not care which model wrote the code

It cares whether the game runs

He took a screenshot of the final Mario build. He prompted Claude to make it darker, faster, and remove the mushroom

That became game 33

The internet said AI cannot ship products that real users will pay for

47 games. 11 weeks. One developer who has never written a real codebase

The store does not need him to be a developer

It just needs him to keep pressing submit

The whole 11-week run cost him less than dinner for two in Shanghai

Save this. The next 1,000 games on the store you have not opened in a year will not be made by studios

author: incognitoprince
text:
You Have Less Than 10 Days To Use The Best AI Ever Made

 Claude Fable 5 Is Here: The Mythos-Class AI That Beat Pokemon, Topped Coding Benchmarks, and Sparked a Pricing Debate 🤖✨

 🚀 The Big Release Everyone Is Talking About

The AI world has a new heavyweight. Claude Fable 5 just dropped, and it is being described as a Mythos-class model meaning it carries the raw capabilities of the powerful Mythos 5, but wrapped in safety restrictions around cybersecurity and biological knowledge. 🛡️ Think of it as the public-facing, safer sibling of one of the most capable AI systems ever built.

So what does that actually mean for developers, businesses, and everyday users? Quite a lot, as it turns out. 👀

 📊 Performance: State-of-the-Art Across the Board

Claude Fable 5 is posting state-of-the-art numbers in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks. But the real story is what happens when tasks get long and complicated. The harder and longer the task, the bigger the gap between Fable 5 and everything else. 📈

On the coding side, it now leads both SweetBench Pro and Frontier Code two of the most respected coding benchmarks in the industry. 🥇 For developers, this is not a small bump. This is leadership territory. 💪

 💰 The Price Tag That Made People Gasp

Here is where the excitement cools down a bit. 😬 API pricing sits at 10 dollars per million input tokens and 50 dollars per million output tokens. That is steep really steep especially for hobby projects or casual experimentation. 💸

There is also a clear shift happening: less generous access through subscriptions, and a stronger push toward usage-based billing. The message is simple: if you want frontier intelligence, you will increasingly pay frontier prices. To justify daily use, your work needs to generate real value. ⚠️
